children: By Cheryl Winokur Munk

The Mather Group has been an active acquirer of registered investment advisor firms in the past several years, integrating multiple RIAs from across the country. The Chicago-based firm, which ranks 41st on Barron's 2026 Top 100 RIA Firms list, has made 25 acquisitions since 2019, often absorbing smaller practices with one or two advisors into a much larger team spread across 14 offices.

"We're looking for RIA partners who share our commitment to clients, their people, and the long-term success of the firm," says Ryan Wickert, the Mather Group's chief financial officer, in a recent Barron's interview. "The right partnership should expand what we can deliver to clients while giving advisors and employees the resources, opportunities, and career paths to grow. Our goal is to build something stronger together."

Jennifer des Groseilliers, the firm's chief executive, and Kristen Oziemkowski, chief operating officer, joined Wickert to discuss how the Mather Group operates, its acquisition strategy, and the integrated services it offers clients. An edited version of the conversation follows.
Barron's: Tell us what's unique about your practice.

Jennifer des Groseilliers: When you work with us, you don't just get one advisor; you get the Mather Group. Our team-based structure matters a lot. I think that is what really differentiates us, especially with the high-net-worth folks we work with. They're looking for a firm that's going to help multiple generations, and we work in a team capacity so they aren't depending on just one advisor.

Kristen Oziemkowski: Our advisors are the quarterbacks of the relationship, but they are surrounded by specialists in financial planning, investments, tax strategy, estate planning, small-business planning, and, for those with assets above $25 million, family office services.
Who are your typical clients?

Oziemkowski: Historically, our core client has been a Fortune 200 executive who is one to two years from retirement or has already retired. That remains an important part of our business, but today we serve a much broader range of clients, including individuals and families, business owners, executives, and ultrahigh-net-worth families.
What is your acquisition strategy?

Ryan Wickert: To date, we've done 25 partnerships across the country, starting in 2019. We're very intentional about our deals so advisors feel like they are partners within TMG, not just someone coming from the outside and operating on an island.

Oziemkowski: Our typical firm at this point has been somewhere from $200 million to $600 million in assets. Most of the firms we've added have been one- or two-person shops, but it varies. We've also partnered with 10- to 12-person shops. The partners we're looking for are client-focused, and their primary focus is on relationships with their clients. So, like the Mather Group, they want to serve their clients very deeply. We are interested in certain geographies across the country, but primarily it's about being a planning-focused company.
What's your stance on giving advisors equity in the firm?

Des Groseilliers: We believe in a total ownership philosophy, which means that every one of our 199 employees either has equity, or they have a path to equity. We believe that really helps our culture, and it drives the commitment to our growth and serving our clients.
What lessons have you learned through your multiple acquisitions?

Des Groseilliers: Our experience has taught us how important it is to stay disciplined about integration. It requires a lot of work and diligence. We do a lot of work up front to make sure we have a partner that has that same desire.

Wickert: When we're having preliminary conversations, we have a level of candor such that the partnership starts before the ink is dry, so to speak. By doing that, we feel like we get way better outcomes.
Oziemkowski: We've also gotten really good at being a lot more transparent when working through things at the front end to ensure really good alignment.
Can you talk about how you've developed family office capabilities to complement the practice?

Wickert: In addition to our Fortune 200-type clients, we also have family office clients that we serve effectively. We have a fully dedicated team that supports our family office, which includes our client service and tax team. Most of the time, conversations turn to family education, family values, charitable giving, and the like. It's a very different type of conversation at those ultra-ultrahigh-net-worth levels. We are able to support these needs with a dedicated team.

Oziemkowski: We're trying to build relationships with spouses, partners, and children of ultrahigh-net-worth clients. There's a different level of complexity and need for clients with $25 million or more. So, we're able to provide very deep estate planning and financial planning services to those clients. Being able to have that in-house with the same integrated approach is definitely a differentiator.
What's keeping clients up at night?

Des Groseilliers: Our clients are thinking about more than what the market or the Federal Reserve might do next. They're asking whether they can retire when they want, maintain their lifestyle, support their families, and feel confident about the decisions they're making. Our role is to help them answer those questions. A strong financial plan isn't built around predicting the next market move. It's built to help clients make informed decisions and stay focused on what they want their wealth to accomplish.

Wickert: Today's environment requires a different level of conversation, since many of our clients are contemplating retirement. But that's where we feel we're earning our keep-to help them understand what retirement looks like or continuing to work looks like under different scenarios. That's why we're here.
Thank you, all.
